ballot_rationales.rationale: Repair changes the material and diff boundary, so validation and review of the superseded state cannot support implementation closure.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The rule is confined to implementation closure; Core marks stale-after-edit evidence and unreviewed changed scope as fail-closed non-completion outcomes.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep closure nonterminal until post-repair validation and review of the latest changed scope are current.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A repair produces a new material state, so validation and review evidence bound to the superseded diff cannot support closure for the repaired result.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Implementation closure after a material repair, as bounded by Review and Repair and the current visible evidence freshness contract.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Mark prior validation and diff-review evidence superseded or invalid; run targeted validation and re-review only for the latest repaired diff.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A repair is a material edit that invalidates the prior validation and review scope, so fresh targeted validation and independent re-review are necessary before implementation closure.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Implementation closure after a material repair, under the review-evidence and closure contracts.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the rule and keep its scope tied to material repairs and the latest diff.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The complete seven-control set preserves authority, safety, formal evidence, targeted validation, independent review, and current completion evidence at every routed level.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Canonical Core enumerates exactly seven non_bypassable controls and L1 retains them all; build and install exact validation provide the stated trust anchor.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain build-install exact validation, the malformed-artifact integrity fallback, and the explicit runtime limits on coordinated tampering and unknown IDs.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The seven controls are explicitly enumerated in the authoritative execution-level contract and protect authority, repository safety, evidence freshness, independent review, and scoped completion at every execution level.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Any routed task governed by the current Core execution_level_contract; the set is the contract's complete non_bypassable array, not a free-standing universal mechanism.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the projected count synchronized with core-contracts; fail authoring validation if its count or content drifts, and re-review after an execution-level contract change.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The execution-level contract enumerates exactly seven controls that remain non-bypassable at every level; applying all seven preserves authorization, evidence freshness, and independent implementation review.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: A valid Level Basis under the generated execution-level contract; its seven-item non-bypassable list is authoritative.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the count-bound rule and regenerate the prompt whenever the authoritative list changes.

ballot_rationales.rationale: One completed path per canonical identity prevents same-path validation loops, while the adjacent gap-or-transition clause admits justified additional evidence paths.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Core validation_loop sets complete_path_limit to one within the validation identity and requires a bound gap or verifiable state transition for another path.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the adjacent exception clause and block repeated completed paths without a canonical uncovered gap or evidence transition.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The limit applies to completed paths for one canonical validation identity, while a declared uncovered gap or verified transition permits another path; it prevents redundant same-identity validation loops rather than capping all validation.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: A completed validation path with unchanged material, scope lineage, effective level, and validation-path identity under the Core validation_loop contract.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Permit a further path only for a bound predeclared uncovered gap or a bound material or external-state transition; otherwise report blocked or partial.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The detected limit of one is a validation-loop cardinality invariant, not a time, cost, service-level, or status threshold; the cited detector family therefore does not apply.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The generated execution-level contract validation_loop.complete_path_limit, governing duplicate completion paths for one validation identity.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the invariant; exclude protocol cardinality fields such as complete_path_limit from this detector family.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A single primary Skill gives each routed task one responsibility and output authority, while optional Layer 3 guidance covers bounded supporting concerns.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The current router routes once per task with one primary Professional Skill; source-free direct answers and utility no-edit work are separately excluded from normal Skill loading.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve route-once assignment and prevent task agents from rerouting or chaining competing primary Professional Skills over the same scope.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A single primary Professional Skill gives a task one authoritative workflow, while named Layer 3 skills supply bounded specialization; this prevents overlapping Professional workflows and task-agent rerouting.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Normal repository task assignment routed once per task under professional-skill-router; utility no-edit modes load no primary Professional Skill.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Select the primary Skill before dispatch, name only capsule-approved Layer 3 additions, and return to the main agent for any route change.

ballot_rationales.rationale: One primary Professional Skill expresses exclusive routing ownership, not a duration, cost, service-level, or status threshold, so the detector family is inapplicable in context.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The Scheduling and Context routing boundary requiring one primary Professional Skill per task.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain exclusive ownership; exempt structural routing-cardinality phrases from the threshold detector.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Writing a diff export into the workspace would mutate the reviewed change set, defeating supplied-artifact scope integrity and no-edit evidence.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: This path applies only when supplied-artifact mode lacks a diff; Core utility rules require diff-export/no-edit output as supplied content or a host-native artifact.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve identical before-and-after workspace checks and invalidate downstream review or closure when comparison evidence changes or is unavailable.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The rule is limited to supplied-artifact review when the actual diff is absent: a no-edit task agent may export the diff as returned content without creating hidden workspace evidence.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: diff_input_mode=supplied-artifact, no actual diff or accessible host-native reference is supplied, and host-enforced utility_no_edit supports task-agent diff export.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Require permitted no-edit diff commands plus unchanged workspace checks; block review with diff scope unverified if export or enforcement is unavailable.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Within supplied-artifact mode, this fallback keeps diff export read-only and prevents review evidence from being created as a persistent workspace file, preserving reviewer independence and evidence provenance.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Only supplied-artifact diff_input_mode when the actual diff is absent and the task-agent runs diff-export/no-edit.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the bounded fallback and continue to block review when diff_input_mode is unsupported.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Formal readiness asserts a stronger evidence boundary, so ordinary authoring validation cannot substantiate that claim without dedicated formal evidence gates.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Core makes formal evidence non-bypassable when formal readiness is declared and repeats that condition as validation_loop.formal_scope_rule.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep formal readiness fail closed until the repository's formal-release evidence succeeds against the final material tree.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Declaring formal readiness changes required rigor but is not evidence that the formal gates passed on the final material tree, so separate formal evidence remains necessary.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Formal release readiness is explicitly in scope under the Core execution_level_contract and the repository's formal-release policy.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Require current formal-release and strict professionalism evidence on the final tree; otherwise withhold formal completion and report the proof limit.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Formal readiness is an explicit scope claim whose evidence cannot be inferred from an ordinary validation path; the formal evidence gate is therefore necessary and correctly conditional.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Only when formal-release readiness is declared in scope, under the execution-level contract's non-bypassable formal-evidence rule.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the conditional gate and distinguish formal evidence from ordinary authoring validation.

limitations: This majority is authoring lifecycle evidence only.
